title: Streamers feeding the SVS13-A protobinary system: astrochemistry reveals accretion shocks?
question: What is the spatial distribution and physical origin of deuterated water (HDO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and formamide (NH2CHO) emission in the SVS13-A protobinary system and its accretion streamer?

data.angular_resolution: ~50 au; 0.19" x 0.13" (PA=+5°) for continuum; 0.21" x 0.14" (207 x 136 mas, PA=+5°) for line cubes
data.sensitivity: 4.8 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1 using 122 kHz (0.15 km s^-1) channels; 8σ = 3.35 mJy beam^-1 in continuum; 5σ = 20 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1 (16 mJy beam^-1 km s^-1 in most blue/red-shifted channels) in channel maps

what.value: NH2CHO 12(1,12)–11(1,11) transition data, integrated intensities, rotational temperatures, column densities, and methanol systemic velocities

evidence.quote: The analysis is supported by the NH 2 CHO 12(1,12)– 11(1,11) transition at 243.521044 GHz, previously published in [1] .
The NH 2 CHO rotational temperatures and column densities derived in [1], are T rot =140 K and N tot =5.9(0.9) × 10 15 cm − 2 in VLA4A and T rot =170 K and N tot =1.4(0.3) × 10 15 cm − 2 in VLA4B.
The central panels correspond to the systemic velocities of VLA4A and VLA4B, which are +7.7 km s − 1 and +8.5 km s − 1, respectively, and have been determined from methanol emission [1] .

what.value: Spectroscopic parameters and frequencies for HDO, SO2, and NH2CHO from JPL and CDMS databases

evidence.quote: Frequencies and spectroscopic parameters have been provided by 31 for HDO, and retrieved from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory molecular database (https://spec.jpl.nasa.gov/) [32] .
For SO 2 spectroscopic parameters are provided by the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (http://www.astro.unikoeln.de/cdms/) [33] .
For NH 2 CHO spectroscopic parameters are provided by [34] and retrieved from the CDMS database.

what.value: Binding energies (BE) of HDO, SO2 and NH2CHO over an amorphous water surface

evidence.quote: Table 2 list the BE of HDO, SO 2 and NH 2 CHO over an amorphous water surface, as computed by [41] and [42] on a ice model of 60 water molecules.

what.value: Pre-exponential factors (ν) of H2O and NH2CHO

evidence.quote: computed by [39] following the [43] formalism (Table 5 of [39] ).

what.value: Grain temperature at 120 au assuming L_bol = 55 L_sun

evidence.quote: The green area shows the grain temperature derived by [44] assuming a bolometric luminosity of 55 L o and a distance from the center of 120 au (see text).

what.value: HDO rotational temperature (150-260 K) and column density (4 x 10^17 cm^-2) from IRAM-30m data

evidence.quote: The HDO line intensity in the brighter source, VLA4A, is consistent with the rotational temperature of 150-260 K and a column density of 4 × 10 17 cm − 2, derived using IRAM-30m data collecting the emission from both protostars [24] .

recipe.goal: Verify continuum streamer structures and map molecular emission
recipe.method: Image 1.2 mm continuum with different beam tapering to verify northern/southern streamers against cleaning artifacts; produce moment 0 maps (integrated over the whole velocity interval) and velocity-binned channel maps for HDO, SO2, and NH2CHO.
key_parameters: SO2 velocity intervals: 6.6-8.7, 8.9-10.4, and 10.5-11.9 km s^-1 (velocities < +6.5 km s^-1 excluded due to CH2DOH contamination)

recipe.goal: Extract spatial intensity profiles and peak integrated intensities
recipe.method: Extract radial and vertical intensity profiles from the moment 0 maps along a horizontal axis connecting VLA4A and VLA4B and a vertical axis crossing the northern streamer; extract velocity-integrated line intensities (in T_MB scale) at the continuum peak positions of VLA4A and VLA4B and compute VLA4A/VLA4B intensity ratios.
key_parameters: Source distance = 299 pc (0.4" corresponds to 120 au)
assumptions: 20% calibration uncertainty included in integrated intensity errors

recipe.goal: Calculate thermal sublimation temperatures and compare with streamer dust temperatures
recipe.method: Compute the half-life time t_sub = ln(2)/k_des and desorption rate k_des = ν_des exp(-BE/T) for HDO, SO2, and NH2CHO over timescales of 10^3 to 10^5 yr using quantum chemical binding energy distributions and pre-exponential factors; compare sublimation curves with expected dust grain temperature at ≥ 120 au.
assumptions: HDO binding energy is equal to that of H2O
BE has a Gaussian distribution of values where the average represents where most molecules thermally sublimate
Spherical envelope-like distribution with L_bol = 55 L_sun at distance ≥ 120 au yields temperature < 100 K

answer_key.quantity: HDO 2(1,1)–2(1,2) velocity integrated line intensity in VLA4A
HDO 2(1,1)–2(1,2) velocity integrated line intensity in VLA4B

evidence.quote: The intensity ratio for HDO is 2.0 (0.6), suggesting that water is distributed in both the protostars, even if it is more abundant in VLA4A.

answer_key.quantity: SO2 5(2,4)–4(1,3) velocity integrated line intensity in VLA4A
SO2 5(2,4)–4(1,3) velocity integrated line intensity in VLA4B
Distance of northern streamer molecular emission from protostars

evidence.quote: Deuterated water reveals an additional emitting component spatially coincident with the dust accretion streamer, at a distance ≥ 120 au from the protostars, and at blue-shifted velocities ( > 3 km s − 1 from the systemic velocities).
The streamer traced by HDO is located at a distance ≥ 120 au from the VLA4A and VLA4B protostars.

answer_key.quantity: Blue-shifted velocity offset of HDO streamer component from systemic velocity

evidence.quote: Deuterated water reveals an additional emitting component spatially coincident with the dust accretion streamer, at a distance ≥ 120 au from the protostars, and at blue-shifted velocities ( > 3 km s − 1 from the systemic velocities).

The overall line distribution confirms what previously reported by [1] but the HDO emission highlights an additional structure (i) with a peak spatially shifted with respect to the protostars position, and (ii) at velocities blue-shifted by ≥ 3 km s − 1 .
The pre-exponential factor of SO 2 was estimated by us using the formalism by [43] .

(2022) [1] and not detailed here, and exact moment-0 integration ranges and profile slice geometries are omitted.
